rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the 80 mm width (x = -0.04 to +0.04 m, step 0.02 m) at y = 0.04 m, ahead of the axle, so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 0.012 m is smaller than the 25 mm tape, so each sensor reads cleanly. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give moderate turn authority. Mass 0.7 kg and a 0.12 m body width keep yaw inertia low and the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m. Controller: sensor weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1] match the signs of x, so a line to the left gives a positive signal and steers left. kp = 5 gives about 350 PWM of differential per 0.2 signal, which should correct a 1 cm offset without saturating. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. kd = 0.1 damps the response a little without amplifying sensor noise. base_speed = 1.4 (about 70 percent PWM) aims for the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving margin for the bends. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with rms_error around 0.02 m. The slalom and sharp bends are the main risk: speed may need to drop there, or kp may need to rise if the robot oscillates.
